title: Al-Kahf 18:1-5: meaning, tadabbur and the rules in detail: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Tajweed mastery and Al-Kahf consolidation
source: Written for quran/y11 lesson 11 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Kahf 18 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 11. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

timeline.text: Praise for Allah who sent down a Book with no deviance
A straight Book: warning and good news of a lasting reward
Warning to those who claim Allah has taken a son: a word without knowledge

panels.title: Meaning guides stopping
points: Stop where a thought is complete

questions.q: In the portal response box, summarise 18:1 to 5 in three sentences (starter: 'Al-Kahf opens by ...').
questions.a: Three accurate sentences matching the three parts.

questions.q: Breakout pairs: recite 18:1 to 5 to a partner who marks every noon rule and the saktah (pupil PDF). Today's rota group recites 18:1 to 5 to the teacher.
questions.a: Partner sheet ticked; teacher records rota scores.

questions.q: Extend: find the other three saktat of Hafs (surah and ayah).
Stretch: explain 'a word without knowledge' (18:5) and why it is serious.
questions.a: A claim about Allah with no proof; speaking about Allah without knowledge is a grave sin.
A) Izhar. Tanween before ح, a throat letter: izhar.

questions.q: Think again: 18:2 gives both a warning and good news. Why do you think the Qur'an so often puts the two together?
questions.a: Fear and hope balance the heart: warning keeps us careful, good news keeps us hopeful.
